candidates.label: target
candidates.comment: A destination relation between an action and its intended entry point or URL. Also called "action destination", "target URL", "entry point for action", "leads to". Examples: "The search action has target a search results page", "The button's target is a specific URL", "This action points to a target entry point."

candidates.label: audience
candidates.comment: An intended group for whom a creative work, event, lodging business, play action, product, or service was created. Also called: target group, demographic, intended recipient. Examples: "CreativeWork 'Children's Book' audience 'Children'", "Event 'Tech Conference' audience 'Developers'", "Product 'Luxury Car' audience 'High-net-worth individuals'."

candidates.label: serviceAudience
candidates.comment: The specific group of people or entities for whom a service is intended or eligible. Also called target audience, service recipients, eligible users. Examples: `Healthcare Service` serviceAudience `Audience: Seniors`, `Educational Service` serviceAudience `Audience: Students`, `Financial Service` serviceAudience `Audience: Small Businesses`.

candidates.label: object
candidates.comment: A thing upon which an action is carried out, potentially changing its state. Also called target, item acted upon, recipient of action. Examples: "Read Action object 'a book'", "Buy Action object 'a product'", "Edit Action object 'a document'". Distinct from instrument, which is the tool used to perform the action.

candidates.label: permitAudience
candidates.comment: A targeting relation between a permit and the specific audience it is intended for. Also called target group, eligible recipients, intended users. Examples: A fishing permit has a permit audience of 'Local Residents'. A building permit has a permit audience of 'Licensed Contractors'. A student permit has a permit audience of 'University Students'.

candidates.label: recipient
candidates.comment: A recipient relation between an action (like sending or paying) and the audience, contact point, organization, or person receiving it. Also called receiver, intended for, sent to. Examples: "A message has a recipient 'John Doe'.", "A donation has a recipient 'Charity Organization'.", "A payment has a recipient 'Vendor Inc.'."

candidates.label: targetCollection
candidates.comment: A specific collection relation between an update action and the collection of things that is the target of the action. Also called "collection to update", "target set", "destination collection". Examples: "The add action has targetCollection a list of items", "The update action's targetCollection is a database table", "This action modifies a targetCollection of documents.". Distinct from object, which is a more general target of an action.

candidates.label: suggestedGender
candidates.comment: An indication of the recommended gender for an intended person or audience. Also called "target gender", "audience gender", "gender recommendation". Examples: "The clothing item has suggestedGender unisex", "The audience specification includes suggestedGender female", "This product is for suggestedGender male."

candidates.label: collection
candidates.comment: A target relation for an update action, indicating the collection that is being updated. Also called "target collection", "updated collection", "collection object". Examples: "Add item update action collection 'Shopping Cart'", "Remove item update action collection 'Wishlist'".

candidates.label: targetPlatform
candidates.comment: An identification of the type of platform for which an API reference is intended, such as phone or desktop. Also called "platform type", "development platform", "operating system target", "device target". Examples: "The API reference has targetPlatform iOS", "The software's targetPlatform is Windows Desktop", "This API is designed for targetPlatform Android."

candidates.label: loser
candidates.comment: A losing participant relation between a win action and the person who lost. Also called: defeated participant, vanquished, runner-up. Examples: "Chess Match WinAction loser Opponent B", "Race WinAction loser Second Place Runner", "Debate WinAction loser Team B".

candidates.label: workPerformed
candidates.comment: A performed work relation between an event and a creative work, indicating that the work is enacted or presented live during the event. Also called enacted work, live presentation, staged work. Examples: TheaterEvent workPerformed "Hamlet", ConcertEvent workPerformed "Symphony No. 5", DancePerformance workPerformed "Swan Lake". Distinct from workFeatured, which is a general showcasing, and workPresented, which is specifically for movies at screening events.

candidates.label: source
candidates.comment: A causal relation between an instantaneous event and the thing that initiated or caused it. Also called "originates from", "caused by", "event trigger", "event origin". Examples: "The explosion's source was a gas leak", "The alarm's source was a smoke detector", "The data breach's source was a phishing attack."

candidates.label: legislationPassedBy
candidates.comment: A passing authority relation between a piece of legislation and the organization or person that originally enacted it. Also called: enacted by, made by, legislated by. Examples: "Primary Legislation legislationPassedBy Parliament", "Secondary Legislation legislationPassedBy Government", "Local Bylaw legislationPassedBy City Council". Distinct from legislationResponsible, which refers to the ministry or individual in charge of elaborating or addressing questions about the legislation.

candidates.label: workFeatured
candidates.comment: A featured work relation between an event and a creative work, indicating that the work is highlighted or showcased within the event. Also called showcased work, highlighted work, exhibited work. Examples: ExhibitionEvent workFeatured PaintingA, FestivalEvent workFeatured SculptureB, ConferenceEvent workFeatured ResearchPaperC. Distinct from workPerformed, which is a live rendition of a work, and workPresented, which is a specific presentation of a movie at a screening event.

candidates.label: causeOf
candidates.comment: A causal relation between a medical cause and the medical entity (condition, complication, symptom) it produces. Also called "results in", "leads to", "produces". Examples: "Influenza virus medical causeOf Flu", "Smoking medical causeOf Lung cancer". Distinct from cause, which describes what leads to a condition, whereas causeOf describes what a medical cause leads to.

candidates.label: deathPlace
candidates.comment: A geographical event relation between a person and the place where they died. Also called: place of demise, passing location, decease location. Examples: "Historical Figure" death place "Dallas, Texas", "Family Member" death place "London, UK". Distinct from birthPlace, which is the place of birth.

candidates.label: supersededBy
candidates.comment: A deprecation relation between an older term (property, class, or enumeration) and a newer term that replaces or supersedes it. Also called "replaced by", "obsoleted by", "succeeded by", "deprecated by". Examples: "OldProperty is supersededBy NewProperty", "The deprecated class is supersededBy a modern equivalent", "This enumeration value is supersededBy a more precise one."

candidates.label: winner
candidates.comment: A winner relation between a losing action and the person who won it. Also called victor, triumphant participant, successful party. Examples: ChessMatchLoseAction winner Alice, RaceLoseAction winner Bob, CompetitionLoseAction winner Charlie.

candidates.label: cause
candidates.comment: A causal relation between a medical condition and its medical cause. Also called "etiology", "origin", "caused by". Examples: "Flu medical condition cause Influenza virus", "Heart attack medical condition cause Coronary artery disease". Distinct from causeOf, which describes what a medical cause leads to, whereas cause describes what leads to a condition.

candidates.label: warning
candidates.comment: A warning relation between a drug and any FDA or other safety advisories. Also called drug warning, safety advisory, health alert. Examples: "Drug warning 'May cause drowsiness.'", "Drug warning 'https://fda.gov/drug-warnings/xyz'", "Medication warning 'Do not exceed recommended dose.'".

candidates.label: foodWarning
candidates.comment: A food warning relation between a drug and any precautions, guidance, or contraindications regarding food consumption while taking it. Also called: dietary restrictions, food interactions, consumption advice. Examples: "Warfarin" food warning "Avoid grapefruit, limit Vitamin K rich foods", "Antibiotics" food warning "Do not take with dairy products", "MAOIs" food warning "Avoid aged cheeses and cured meats".

candidates.label: alcoholWarning
candidates.comment: An alcohol warning relation between a drug and any precautions or contraindications regarding alcohol consumption while using it. Also called alcohol interaction, drinking advisory, alcohol caution. Examples: "A medication's alcohol warning states 'Do not consume alcohol'.", "The drug's alcohol warning advises 'Limit alcohol intake'."

candidates.label: pregnancyWarning
candidates.comment: A medical attribute providing precautions, guidance, or contraindications regarding a drug's use during pregnancy. Also called pregnancy precautions, drug-pregnancy risks, maternal warnings. Examples: A drug has a pregnancy warning 'Consult doctor before use'. The medication includes a pregnancy warning about 'potential fetal harm'. There is a pregnancy warning against 'use in first trimester'.

candidates.label: breastfeedingWarning
candidates.comment: Any precaution, guidance, or contraindication related to a drug's use by breastfeeding mothers. Also called: lactation warning, nursing caution, breastfeeding safety. Examples: "Drug 'Medication X' breastfeedingWarning 'Consult doctor before use'", "Drug 'Drug Y' breastfeedingWarning 'Not recommended for breastfeeding mothers'."

candidates.label: contraindication
candidates.comment: A medical restriction relation for a medical device or therapy, indicating a contraindication. Also called "medical warning", "precaution", "not recommended for". Examples: "Drug therapy contraindication 'Pregnancy'", "Medical device contraindication 'Pacemaker users'".

candidates.label: safetyConsideration
candidates.comment: Any potential safety concerns, interactions, or adverse reactions associated with a dietary supplement. Also called supplement warnings, safety warnings, adverse effects. Examples: `St. John's Wort` safetyConsideration `"May interact with antidepressants"`, `Creatine Supplement` safetyConsideration `"Not recommended for individuals with kidney issues"`, `Vitamin D Supplement` safetyConsideration `"Avoid excessive dosage"`.

candidates.label: expertConsiderations
candidates.comment: An expert considerations relation between a diet and the medical expert advice pertinent to that dietary plan. Also called: medical advice, professional guidance, health warnings. Examples: "Keto Diet" expert considerations "Consult a doctor if you have kidney issues", "Vegan Diet" expert considerations "Ensure adequate B12 supplementation", "Low-Sodium Diet" expert considerations "Monitor blood pressure regularly".

candidates.label: accessibilityHazard
candidates.comment: An accessibility hazard relation between a creative work and a characteristic that poses a physiological danger to some users. Also called accessibility risk, dangerous feature, user hazard. Examples: "A video's accessibility hazard is 'flashingLights'.", "A game's accessibility hazard is 'motionSimulation'."

candidates.label: risks
candidates.comment: The specific physiological dangers or adverse effects associated with a particular diet plan. Also called diet hazards, health risks of diet, diet side effects. Examples: `Keto Diet` risks `"Nutrient deficiencies"`, `Fad Diet` risks `"Metabolic imbalance"`, `Vegan Diet` risks `"Vitamin B12 deficiency if not supplemented"`.

candidates.label: startDate
candidates.comment: A temporal marker indicating the beginning date and time of an item, such as an event, program, or season. Also called "beginning date", "commencement date", "start time", "effective date". Examples: "The event has startDate 2023-10-26", "The program's startDate is September 1st", "This role's startDate was last Monday.". Distinct from dateCreated, which indicates when a creative work was first made.

candidates.label: deathDate
candidates.comment: A temporal event relation between a person and their date of death. Also called: date of demise, passing date, decease date. Examples: "Historical Figure" death date "1963-11-22", "Family Member" death date "2020-05-10". Distinct from birthDate, which is the date of birth.

candidates.label: previousStartDate
candidates.comment: A temporal attribute indicating the previously scheduled start date for an event that has been rescheduled or cancelled. Also called original start date, former start date, initial event date. Examples: A rescheduled event has a previous start date of '2023-03-15'. The cancelled concert had a previous start date of '2023-07-01T19:00:00'. The postponed meeting's previous start date was 'last Monday'. Distinct from startDate, which is the current or newly scheduled start date.

candidates.label: byDay
candidates.comment: A temporal specification for a schedule, indicating the day(s) of the week on which a recurring event occurs. Also called "days of week", "weekly recurrence", "on day". Examples: "Weekly meeting schedule byDay Monday", "Class schedule byDay 'MO,WE,FR'".

candidates.label: contentReferenceTime
candidates.comment: A temporal reference relation for a creative work, indicating the specific date and time described or emphasized within its content. Also called "event time", "depicted time", "time of content". Examples: "News article contentReferenceTime '2023-10-26T14:00:00Z'", "Historical documentary contentReferenceTime '1945-09-02'".

candidates.label: follows
candidates.comment: A follows relation representing a generic uni-directional social connection between two people. Also called: is following, subscribes to, tracks. Examples: "Alice follows Bob", "Charlie follows David", "Eve follows Frank". Distinct from followee, which is the object of a follow action.

candidates.label: source
candidates.comment: A causal relation between an instantaneous event and the thing that initiated or caused it. Also called "originates from", "caused by", "event trigger", "event origin". Examples: "The explosion's source was a gas leak", "The alarm's source was a smoke detector", "The data breach's source was a phishing attack."

candidates.label: temporal
candidates.comment: A general temporal relation between a creative work and a date or time, used when more specific temporal properties are not applicable. Also called "related to time", "time context", "associated temporal period", "timeframe". Examples: "The novel has temporal the 19th century", "The painting's temporal is the Renaissance era", "This document's temporal is the year 2020.". Distinct from temporalCoverage, which indicates the specific time period the content applies to.

candidates.label: startOffset
candidates.comment: A temporal offset indicating the start time of a clip or action, measured in seconds from the beginning of a larger work. Also called "clip start time", "beginning offset", "time offset start", "seek start". Examples: "The video clip has startOffset 30 seconds", "The action's startOffset is 120 seconds into the recording", "This segment begins at startOffset 0."

candidates.label: departureTime
candidates.comment: A temporal event relation between a trip and its expected departure time. Also called: scheduled departure, leaving time, takeoff time. Examples: "Flight" departure time "2023-11-01T08:00:00Z", "Bus Trip" departure time "14:30:00", "Train Journey" departure time "2023-12-25T10:00:00". Distinct from arrivalTime, which is the expected arrival time.

candidates.label: eventAttendanceMode
candidates.comment: An event attendance mode relation between an event and the enumeration indicating whether it occurs online, offline, or a mix. Also called "attendance format", "event delivery mode", "participation mode". Examples: "Event 'Conference' eventAttendanceMode 'OnlineEventAttendanceMode'", "Event 'Workshop' eventAttendanceMode 'OfflineEventAttendanceMode'", "Event 'Hybrid Meeting' eventAttendanceMode 'MixedEventAttendanceMode'".

candidates.label: availabilityEnds
candidates.comment: A date or time marking the end of availability for a product or service in an offer or access specification. Also called: availability end date, offer expiration, access end time. Examples: "Offer 'Sale Item' availabilityEnds '2023-12-31'", "ActionAccessSpecification 'Early Bird' availabilityEnds '2023-10-30T23:59:59'". Distinct from availabilityStarts, which marks the beginning.

candidates.label: isPlanForApartment
candidates.comment: A descriptive relation between a floor plan and the accommodation unit it illustrates. Also called plan for, describes accommodation, layout for. Examples: A floor plan isPlanForApartment 'Apartment 3B'. A floor plan isPlanForApartment 'a studio apartment'. A floor plan isPlanForApartment 'Unit 101'.

candidates.label: accommodationFloorPlan

Examples: "A hotel suite's accommodation floor plan shows two bedrooms.", "The residence's accommodation floor plan includes a garage."

candidates.label: scheduledTime
candidates.comment: The specific date or date and time when an action is planned to occur. Also called planned time, scheduled date, appointment time. Examples: `Meeting Action` scheduledTime `2023-10-26T10:00:00`, `Delivery Action` scheduledTime `2023-11-01`, `Maintenance Action` scheduledTime `2023-12-05T14:30:00`.

candidates.label: exercisePlan
candidates.comment: An exercise plan relation between an exercise action and the specific plan or routine followed during the action. Also called: workout routine, training regimen, fitness program. Examples: "Morning Run" exercise plan "Couch to 5K Plan", "Weightlifting Session" exercise plan "StrongLifts 5x5", "Yoga Practice" exercise plan "Beginner Vinyasa Flow".

candidates.label: scheduledPaymentDate
candidates.comment: The specific date on which an invoice is planned or expected to be paid. Also called payment due date, invoice due date, planned payment date. Examples: `Invoice #123` scheduledPaymentDate `2023-12-31`, `Utility Bill` scheduledPaymentDate `2024-01-15`, `Consulting Invoice` scheduledPaymentDate `2023-11-30`. Distinct from `paymentDueDate`, which is a more general term for when payment is due.

candidates.label: includesHealthPlanNetwork
candidates.comment: A health plan network inclusion relation between a health insurance plan and a network it covers. Also called plan network, covered network, network of plan. Examples: "A health insurance plan includes a health plan network.", "The plan covers an includes health plan network.", "This insurance plan features a specific network."

candidates.label: itinerary
candidates.comment: A travel plan relation between a trip and the sequence of places or an item list detailing the destinations. Also called travel route, trip plan, destinations, journey path. Examples: A trip has an itinerary of 'Paris, Rome, London'. A trip has an itinerary of an ItemList detailing stops. A vacation package has an itinerary of 'Hawaii'.

candidates.label: healthPlanMarketingUrl
candidates.comment: A health plan marketing URL relation between a health insurance plan and the direct URL to its plan brochure. Also called plan brochure URL, marketing link, plan details URL. Examples: "A health insurance plan has a health plan marketing URL.", "The plan's marketing URL leads to its brochure.", "This insurance plan provides a health plan marketing URL."

candidates.label: negativeNotes

candidates.label: possibleComplication

candidates.label: musicBy

candidates.label: reviewedBy

candidates.label: readBy

candidates.label: participant
candidates.comment: A collaborative relation between an action and an organization or person who indirectly participated in it. Also called collaborated with, involved, assisted by, co-agent. Examples: A writing action has a participant co-author. A research project has a participant researcher. A meeting has a participant attendee. candidates.label: hasParticipationOffer
candidates.comment: A participation offer relation between an event and an offer to participate in it. Also called call for participation, participation opportunity, event entry offer. Examples: "An event has a participation offer for speakers.", "The conference has a participation offer for proposals.", "This festival includes a participation offer for performers.". Distinct from hasSponsorshipOffer, which is an offer to sponsor the event.

candidates.label: sportsTeam

Examples: "The goal was scored by the sportsTeam Real Madrid", "The race involved sportsTeam Team USA", "This action was performed by a sportsTeam.". Distinct from participant, which is a more general participant property.

candidates.label: competitor
candidates.comment: A participation relation in a sports event, indicating a person or sports team that is competing. Also called "participant", "opponent", "rival". Examples: "Olympic race sports event competitor Usain Bolt", "Football match sports event competitor Manchester United".

candidates.label: performerIn
candidates.comment: A participation role relation between a person and an event in which they perform or participate. Also called performs in, participates in, acts in, presents at. Examples: John Doe is a performer in 'The Annual Gala'. Jane Smith is a performer in 'The City Marathon'. An actor is a performer in 'The New Play'. Distinct from performer, which points from an event to a person.

candidates.label: contributor
candidates.comment: A secondary participation relation for a creative work or event, indicating an organization or person who contributed to it. Also called "additional contributor", "supporting role", "collaborator". Examples: "Book creative work contributor 'Editor Jane Doe'", "Conference event contributor 'Sponsor Acme Corp'". Distinct from author or creator, which typically denote primary responsibility.

candidates.label: performer
candidates.comment: A participation role relation between an event and an organization or person who performs at it. Also called artist, entertainer, presenter, actor. Examples: A concert has a performer 'Taylor Swift'. A play has a performer 'Meryl Streep'. A conference has a performer 'Dr. Jane Doe'. Distinct from performerIn, which points from a person to an event.

candidates.label: eventAttendanceMode
candidates.comment: An event attendance mode relation between an event and the enumeration indicating whether it occurs online, offline, or a mix. Also called "attendance format", "event delivery mode", "participation mode". Examples: "Event 'Conference' eventAttendanceMode 'OnlineEventAttendanceMode'", "Event 'Workshop' eventAttendanceMode 'OfflineEventAttendanceMode'", "Event 'Hybrid Meeting' eventAttendanceMode 'MixedEventAttendanceMode'".

candidates.label: attendee
candidates.comment: A person or organization present at an event. Also called: participant, guest, visitor. Examples: "Event 'Concert' attendee 'John Doe'", "Event 'Conference' attendee 'Acme Corp'", "Event 'Meeting' attendee 'Jane Smith'". Distinct from attendees, which is the plural form.

candidates.label: performers
candidates.comment: A participation role relation between an event and its primary performers, who can be organizations or persons. Also called main artists, headliners, principal actors, featured performers. Examples: A concert has performers 'Coldplay'. A play has performers 'The Royal Shakespeare Company'. A festival has performers 'Various Artists'. Distinct from performer, which can be any performer, not necessarily the main one.

candidates.label: hasRepresentation
candidates.comment: A representation relation between a biochemical entity and its common symbolic or structural representation. Also called represented by, symbolic form, structural representation. Examples: "A BioChemEntity has a representation as a chemical structure.", "The entity has a representation as a text sequence.", "This biochemical entity has a URL representation."

candidates.label: about
candidates.comment: A subject matter relation between an entity (e.g., a creative work, event, or communication) and the topic it concerns. Also called concerning, regarding, on the topic of, related to. Examples: "A book about quantum physics.", "A lecture about climate change.", "A certification about data privacy."

candidates.label: sender
candidates.comment: The audience, organization, or person initiating and transmitting a message or action. Also called originator, dispatcher, message source, sender of message. Examples: `Email Message` sender `John Doe`, `ReceiveAction` sender `Customer Service`, `Broadcast Message` sender `News Organization`. Distinct from `recipient`, which is the receiving party.

candidates.label: item
candidates.comment: A list element relation between a data feed item or list item and the entity it represents within a collection. Also called represents, refers to, entry, element. Examples: A list item has an item of 'John Doe'. A data feed item has an item of 'Product X'. A list entry has an item of 'Event Y'.

candidates.label: interpretedAsClaim
candidates.comment: A claim extraction relation between a creative work or media object and a specific assertion or statement derived from its content. Also called contains claim, implies claim, claim extracted from, claim derived from. Examples: A news article is interpretedAsClaim 'The sky is blue'. A scientific paper is interpretedAsClaim 'Drug X cures Y'. A video is interpretedAsClaim 'Candidate Z made promise A'.

candidates.label: hasCertification
candidates.comment: A certification relation between an entity (organization, person, place, product, or service) and its associated certification. Also called holds certification, certified by, possesses certification, has accreditation. Examples: "An organization has a certification for quality management.", "A product has a certification for organic ingredients.", "A person has a certification in project management."

candidates.label: acquiredFrom
candidates.comment: An acquired from relation between ownership information and the organization or person from whom a product was obtained. Also called purchased from, obtained from, source of acquisition. Examples: "The car's ownership info indicates it was acquired from 'Dealership X'.", "The book's ownership info shows it was acquired from 'John Doe'."

candidates.label: encoding
candidates.comment: An encoding relation between a creative work and a media object that represents or contains it. Also called "represented by media", "media representation", "has media object". Examples: "Movie 'The Matrix' encoding 'Matrix.mp4'", "Song 'Bohemian Rhapsody' encoding 'BohemianRhapsody.mp3'", "Book '1984' encoding '1984.epub'". Distinct from encodesCreativeWork, which is the inverse relation (MediaObject -> CreativeWork).

candidates.label: contactPoints
candidates.comment: A communication relation between an organization or person and their various contact points. Also called "contact information", "points of contact", "ways to reach". Examples: "Company organization contactPoints [Customer Service, Press Office]", "Person contactPoints [Email, Phone]". Distinct from contactPoint, which is the singular form, though semantically similar.

candidates.label: itemReviewed
candidates.comment: A review subject relation between an aggregate rating or review and the entity that is being evaluated or rated. Also called reviewed item, rated item, subject of review, evaluated entity. Examples: A review has an itemReviewed of 'Restaurant X'. An aggregate rating has an itemReviewed of 'Movie Y'. A product review has an itemReviewed of 'Smartphone Z'. Distinct from itemOffered, which is the subject of an offer or demand.

relations.definition: Specifies the geographical location of an event.
relations.embedding_query_text: location: Specifies the geographical location of an event.

instances: NATO summit in Ankara -> Ankara

chosen_property.label: location
chosen_property.justification: The 'location' property (Event → Place) directly matches ConferenceEvent → City as the event's location.

candidates.label: location
candidates.comment: A location relation between an action, event, interaction counter, or organization and its physical or virtual place. Also called: situated at, takes place at, found at. Examples: "Conference Event location New York Hilton", "Company Organization location 123 Main St", "Online Meeting location Virtual Conference Room".

candidates.label: deathPlace
candidates.comment: A geographical event relation between a person and the place where they died. Also called: place of demise, passing location, decease location. Examples: "Historical Figure" death place "Dallas, Texas", "Family Member" death place "London, UK". Distinct from birthPlace, which is the place of birth.

candidates.label: geo
candidates.comment: A geo relation between a place and its geographical coordinates or shape. Also called: geographic location, coordinates, spatial data. Examples: "Eiffel Tower" geo "Latitude: 48.8584, Longitude: 2.2945", "Central Park" geo "Polygon GeoShape", "Mount Everest" geo "Point GeoCoordinates".

candidates.label: locationCreated
candidates.comment: A creation location relation between a creative work and the place where it was created. Also called: place of creation, origin location, created in. Examples: "Painting locationCreated Paris", "Novel locationCreated London", "Film locationCreated Hollywood". Distinct from location, which refers to the current or general location of an entity.

candidates.label: spatial
candidates.comment: A general spatial relation between a creative work and a place, used when more specific location properties are not applicable. Also called "related to place", "takes place in", "associated location", "geographic context". Examples: "The novel has spatial Paris", "The painting's spatial is a rural landscape", "This document's spatial is the Amazon rainforest.". Distinct from spatialCoverage, which indicates the specific geographic focus of the content.

candidates.label: longitude
candidates.comment: A longitude relation between geographic coordinates or a place and its longitudinal value. Also called: geographic longitude, east-west coordinate, meridian position. Examples: "Eiffel Tower longitude 2.2945", "Statue of Liberty longitude -74.0445", "Mount Everest longitude 86.9250".

candidates.label: announcementLocation
candidates.comment: An announcement location relation between a special announcement and the specific civic structure or local business it pertains to. Also called relevant location, associated place, specific venue. Examples: "A special announcement's announcement location is 'City Hall'.", "The emergency announcement's announcement location is 'Local Grocery Store'." Distinct from spatialCoverage, which is used for larger geographic regions.

candidates.label: latitude
candidates.comment: A geographical coordinate relation between geo-coordinates or a place and its north-south position on the Earth's surface. Also called lat, north-south coordinate, parallel. Examples: GeoCoordinates have a latitude of '34.0522'. A place has a latitude of '-33.8688'. The city's latitude is '40.7128'. Distinct from longitude, which is the east-west position.

candidates.label: studyLocation
candidates.comment: A geographic relation between a medical study and the administrative area where it is conducted or was conducted. Also called "research location", "trial site", "study area", "geographic scope of study". Examples: "The medical study has studyLocation New York", "The clinical trial's studyLocation is Europe", "This study is taking place in a specific studyLocation."

candidates.label: sportsActivityLocation
candidates.comment: A specific location relation between an exercise action and the sports activity venue where it took place. Also called "exercise location", "training venue", "athletic facility", "gym location". Examples: "The run had sportsActivityLocation Central Park", "The workout's sportsActivityLocation was the local gym", "This exercise action took place at a sportsActivityLocation stadium.". Distinct from location, which is a more general location property.
